name: ryu.blueprint
description: Review an agent's plan before it touches a file. The agent publishes its plan over MCP; Blueprint parses the markdown into addressable blocks and renders it next to a dependency graph derived from the steps' own `depends_on` edges — so the two questions a wall of markdown cannot answer become visible at a glance: what actually has to happen first, and which step is the one everything else is waiting on. A plan reads as a sequence because prose is a sequence; the work almost never is. You annotate what you object to, anchored to the block or step it belongs to — a comment, a redline carrying the replacement text you want, a question, or a blocker — and then approve or request changes. The verdict is not a mood: it is a document. Requesting changes serializes every annotation into deterministic text the agent reads back through `blueprint__plan_status`, each finding naming the step or block it attaches to and, for a redline, the exact substitution proposed, so a revision answers what was actually written rather than what a summary of it sounded like. Re-publishing under the same plan id appends a revision instead of creating a new plan, and block ids are content-stable across revisions, so the second draft arrives as a diff against the first — the paragraphs you already read are still the paragraphs you already read.

blueprint.description: Publish a plan for a human to review, and read the verdict back as text. Reach for this before a change that is expensive to undo — a migration, a refactor across many files, anything where the wrong first step wastes the rest. `plan_publish` posts numbered steps with their `depends_on` edges and returns a review url; `plan_status` polls for the verdict with a bounded wait and returns the reviewer's annotations already serialized into readable findings; `plan_get` fetches the whole plan with its annotations; `step_update` marks a step done as the work lands, so the reviewer watching the graph sees progress without being asked.
